ONE DESIGN FACT THE PLAN COULD NOT HAVE KNOWN, and it is why ensureSeededGoal exists: the two bootstrap seeders DISAGREE about goals. `driveThrough` (bootstrap-test-fixtures) runs goal.create; `seedReadyProject` (recovery/restore-test-harness) runs only register/bind_repository/probe/activate and NEVER creates a goal. That is exactly the measured 265-vs-6 ratio -- the graph is missing everywhere, the goal only sometimes. Re-sending goal.create into a world that has one would refuse on aggregate version, so the guard is a PRECONDITION (`store.readEvents(GOAL_ID).length > 0`), not a swallowed error: any other refusal still throws with its code.

THE NINE POSITIVE CONTROLS, all read back through COMMITTED production readers (readCurrentActiveGraph, readCurrentBudgetLedger) -- never a test-local accessor:
  graph:    exactly one ACTIVE revision at the expected id, provenance.goalRef == GOAL_ID
            EXACT execution-bearing count (toHaveLength 1) + the node key -- `> 0` was rejected on purpose: an empty graph satisfies `> 0` vacuously because there is nothing to count
            graphContentHash equals the content the seed returned (the projection is not reading a headless revision)
  budget:   authorization.amounts reads back as [{ meter: runner.authorized_ms, amount: 1_000_000 }]
            every root meter is a MEMBER of NODE_ADMISSION_METERS (the frozen 7-list)
            root meter set EQUALS the seeded node definitions' admissionAmounts meter set -- BOTH OPERANDS READ BACK FROM DURABLE RECORDS, neither is the literal the fixture wrote. Membership alone is insufficient and I state why in the test: a root funded on `attempt.count` is a member and still has zero coverage for a node denominated in runner.authorized_ms.
  negative: no-graph world -> ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT @ ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION
            no-graph world -> BUDGET_PROJECTION_GRAPH_UNAVAILABLE @ BUDGET_CURRENT_PROJECTION  (the 265-hit code keeps a home)
            no-goal  world -> BUDGET_PROJECTION_GOAL_ABSENT @ BUDGET_CURRENT_PROJECTION  (the 6-hit code; a DIFFERENT readBudgetBinding branch, so neither can answer for the other)
  Every refusal asserts code AND layer as a tuple (global rail 1 / epic rail 6).

NOT YET PROVEN, and I am not claiming it here: that these nine would RED on a wrong seed. Green-on-first-run is not evidence an assertion is attached. comments.author: qa-6c108bfc
comments.content:
QA note for this row's PLANNER, filed before planning rather than at the gate. Re-filed from chat (msg-4a71f3ab, empty routing receipt).

THE STATED GATE IS TOO WEAK, AND IT IS WEAK FOR THE REASON THE ROW LOOKS SAFE. The row is described as "a strict no-op under today's code, gate = 185 files / 4062 tests still green". Both halves are true and together they are the problem: if the row is a no-op today, a green suite CANNOT distinguish a correct seed from a wrong one. Nothing reads the durable ACTIVE graph or the authorized budget root yet - that is what no-op means - so a seeder that plants an empty graph, a graph with zero execution-bearing nodes, a budget root in the wrong meter vocabulary, or one that silently fails to seed at all, all produce the identical 185/4062 green. The row's value is realised in a LATER row (e194c5f6 step 6) and its gate can only observe the present. Step 6 then fails again with a different reason code while this row is already DONE.

NEEDED: A POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE SEED'S EFFECT, not a regression check.
1. Read the seeded world back THROUGH PRODUCTION READERS: readCurrentActiveGraph(store, projectId) returns an ACTIVE graph at the expected revision, and the budget projection returns a root authorized in NODE_ADMISSION_METERS vocabulary (attempt.count, provider.*, runner.authorized_ms, verification.authorized_ms) - NOT ledger vocabulary. That second clause is a live seam measured on e194c5f6: the ledger meter is a bounded free string and the shared budget-transition-fixtures.ts authorizes roots on tokens/seconds, so a root funded that way has no durable coverage for the meter a node definition actually spends. Such a world seeds green and refuses at reserve time.
2. VACUITY GUARD ON THE SWEEP: assert the shared seeding helper was actually invoked in each of the ~14 seeders. Rail 6: "a sweep that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing."
3. PRESERVE ONE NEGATIVE SEEDER ON PURPOSE. If all ~14 seeders get the happy precondition from one helper, BUDGET_PROJECTION_GRAPH_UNAVAILABLE (265 hits when step 6 ran) and GOAL_ABSENT (6) lose their only coverage in the daemon - a guard downstream of a normalizing fixture, green forever and killable by deleting the check. At least one seeder must keep the no-graph shape with a comment saying it is deliberate, and the refusal arm must assert the code AND the layer per rail 6.

SCOPE: name every seeder path in affectedFiles at filing time, including the UNOWNED tests/security/*.ts seeders. Rail 3 permits only explicit owned paths, so an unnamed seeder cannot be touched by the worker and the same 413-test wall reappears when e194c5f6 step 6 is retried.

Being the cheapest of the three PLANNING rows is an argument for planning it FIRST, not for gating it lightly: the risk is not that it breaks something today, it is that it certifies nothing and that surfaces two rows later.
